forecasts.question: Will AGI be developed before 1 January 2030?
forecasts.key_change: Hold at 27% (CI unchanged [14,41]). Two roughly offsetting developments in the 3-4 August window. First, the ARC-AGI-3 evidence that contributed to yesterday's +1 move has been substantially deflated: coverage on 3 August (MLQ News, The Decoder, Softonic) reports that under the official ARC Prize standardized harness GPT-5.6 Sol scores only 7.78% on the public set - the 38.3% figure is OpenAI's self-reported rerun using proprietary Responses API settings ('Retained Reasoning' plus 'Compaction'), unverified on the private set, and Chollet's distinction between barred custom harnesses and permissible general-purpose API settings remains unresolved. Opus 5's 30.2% stands as official SOTA, so the 'two labs traded SOTA in a week' story priced yesterday was really a harness dispute, not a clean second capability jump; that alone would argue -1. Offsetting it is a genuinely strong new capability datapoint crossing into resolution-relevant territory: an OpenAI reasoning model disproved a 1946 Erdős unit-distance conjecture in discrete geometry for ~$2,000 of compute, and Fields Medalist Timothy Gowers wrote he would recommend the paper for the Annals of Mathematics 'without any hesitation' (OpenAI announcement, covered by The Decoder and The Conversation, 1-2 Aug). Verifiable original research endorsed by elite mathematicians is precisely the kind of evidence that moves leading researchers toward eventual AGI declarations, worth roughly +1. On governance, the picture also nets to zero: NBC News (3 Aug) confirms the Pacing the Frontier statement now carries 1,000+ signatures including the chief scientists of Anthropic (Kaplan), OpenAI (Pachocki) and Meta (Zhao) - formalizing the anti-declaration norm at the top of every major lab - while The Information reports the lapsed EO 14409 framework is 'close to final with drafts exchanged', suggesting the machinery yesterday's forecast marked as stalled is proceeding privately. No lab announcement or researcher declaration activity detected; no trigger conditions met. Net: hold.
forecasts.base_rate: Reference class: expert and market forecasts for announcement-based AGI within ~3.4 years. Prediction markets in late July 2026 put ~10% on OpenAI achieving AGI by 2027; Metaculus-style aggregates for weak/announced AGI cluster medians in the early-to-mid 2030s, implying roughly 20-30% mass before 2030; AAAI 2025 survey found 76% of AI researchers doubt pure scaling reaches AGI. Historical base rate of confidently predicted transformative-tech milestones arriving on schedule is low (fusion, FSD), arguing against the high end.

factors_up.factor: OpenAI model disproved a 1946 Erdős conjecture for ~$2,000 compute; Gowers says Annals-worthy 'without hesitation' - first clear crossing from benchmarks into verifiable original research
Frontier scaffolding gains real even if disputed: Sol's 38.3% with retained reasoning/compaction suggests large inference-time headroom on generality tasks
EO 14409 framework still unpublished past its 1 Aug deadline; voluntary regime with no legal consequence for slippage

factors_down.factor: ARC-AGI-3 official verified score for GPT-5.6 Sol is 7.78%, not 38.3%; Opus 5's 30.2% remains SOTA and yesterday's 'second SOTA jump' is a contested harness dispute
Pacing the Frontier now formally signed by chief scientists of Anthropic, OpenAI and Meta plus 1,000+ lab employees - institutionalized norm against racing to and declaring AGI
Definitional gatekeeping remains strict: Huang's March claim still widely rebutted; 3+ leading-researcher bar policed hard
Anthropic disclosed eval-security incidents (unauthorized model access to partner systems), reinforcing lab caution on autonomous deployment

key_uncertainties: Whether the near-final EO 14409 framework, once published, hardens into de facto mandatory pre-release review with lab compliance
Whether the ARC Prize adjudicates OpenAI's retained-reasoning settings as legitimate, and whether scaffolding-driven gains generalize to open-ended autonomy
Whether AI-originated mathematical results (Erdős disproof) start a cascade of elite-researcher statements that AGI-level research capability has arrived
Whether the resolution bar (lab announcement or 3+ leading researchers) drifts as commercial incentives to declare AGI grow
update_triggers: Revise UP if ARC Prize validates the 38.3% methodology or any frontier lab scores >60% on ARC-AGI-3 under official settings
Revise UP if AI systems produce multiple independently-verified novel research results across fields, or elite researchers begin publicly framing this as AGI-level
Revise UP if a major lab reframes its next flagship as 'AGI-class' or the EO 14409 framework is formally abandoned
Revise DOWN if the published EO 14409 framework establishes functioning pre-release review with broad lab compliance
Revise DOWN if Pacing the Frontier converts into binding international pacing mechanisms
Revise DOWN if 2027 flagship models show clearly diminishing returns on generality benchmarks under standardized evaluation

forecasts.question: Will economic consultancy lose ≥33% value/jobs by end 2030 due to AI?
forecasts.key_change: Hold at 22%. Today's task was verifying yesterday's two flagged items against primary sources, and both partially deflate on inspection. (1) The 'EY UK senior consulting cuts' story circulating this weekend traces to Bloomberg Tax, City AM and consultancy.uk reports of ~150 roles (managers/senior managers/directors) — but that is a December 2024 story, affecting only ~3% of EY's 4,700-strong UK consulting arm, attributed to soft advisory demand and a 4% consulting revenue fall, not primarily to AI. As a 'senior second wave' AI signal it is weaker than it appeared in weekend aggregators. (2) Deloitte's title overhaul is confirmed by Fortune (22 Jan 2026): scrapping analyst-consultant-manager titles for ~181,500 US staff effective 1 June 2026, explicitly framed around AI reshaping the pyramid and its $3bn GenAI commitment — real and AI-linked, but a re-titling exercise, not a headcount or revenue decline, so it does not move the resolution needle. Searches on 3-4 Aug surfaced no new trigger-level events: the running tally is unchanged (McKinsey ~10%/3,000-4,000 cuts concentrated in back-office and junior research, Accenture 11,000 roles under its $865m AI restructuring with headcount 791k to 779k May-Aug 2026, KPMG ~400 US advisory). One genuinely useful new datapoint is Revelio Labs' job-postings analysis showing consulting talent demand ~20% below its 2023 peak and consultant-role postings ~40% lower — a leading indicator of structural pyramid compression, though hiring demand is not employment, and it roughly offsets the deflated EY signal. Countervailing revenue picture unchanged: Source Global Research still sees tech consulting passing $400bn (+7%) in 2026 and the MCA projects UK sector growth of 5.7% in 2026 and 7.4% in 2027. Net: signals cancel; hold at 22, CI [11,36].
forecasts.base_rate: Reference class: major professional-services sectors hit by prior automation waves (audit post-digitisation, legal discovery post-e-discovery, IT services post-offshoring). None lost ≥33% of revenue or employment within six years of the technology shock; the typical pattern is 10-20% junior-role pyramid compression alongside top-line growth from selling the disruptive technology as a service. Base rate for a ≥33% sector-wide contraction attributed primarily to a single technology within ~6 years: well under 15%; consulting's current AI-revenue offset argues for the low end.

factors_up.factor: AI-linked headcount rationalisation continuing at scale: McKinsey ~10% (3,000-4,000 roles), Accenture 11,000 roles under $865m AI restructuring, KPMG ~400 US advisory cuts

High resolution bar: ≥33% decline from 2024 baseline plus 2+ credible analyses attributing it primarily to AI; current cuts are demand- and mix-attributed as much as AI-attributed (e.g. EY UK cuts blamed on soft demand)

The one genuinely new data point is the first Clacton constituency poll (Survation for Mandate Research, reported 2 Aug): Farage on ~73% with novelty candidate Count Binface second on ~20% in a race the major parties are boycotting - a foregone coronation carrying essentially zero information about the national race, exactly as assumed yesterday. With the evidence base unchanged, the calibrated response is to hold: the Burnham honeymoon logic (a 2-3pp lead, 3.5 years out, historically fragile) still caps Labour near coin-flip territory, and the CI stays wide at [34,63] pending the Clacton result (13 Aug) and the next round of national polls.
forecasts.base_rate: Reference class: post-war UK governing parties seeking re-election retained most seats in roughly 11 of 20 contests (~55%), but polling 3+ years out has weak predictive power (Major 1990-92 and Blair mid-terms saw >10pp swings). In a fragmented three-way race under FPTP (Lab/Ref/Con all at 20-26%), seat outcomes are hypersensitive to small vote shifts, arguing for probabilities near 40-55% for the current polling leader. Sources: House of Commons Library CBP-8647; PollCheck/BritPolls aggregates.

forecasts.question: Will AGI be developed before 1 January 2035?
forecasts.key_change: Hold at 86%. The 3-4 August news window contained nothing that moves an 8.4-year forecast. (1) The one live capability story matured rather than advanced: OpenAI's 30 July claim that GPT-5.6 Sol scores 38.3% on ARC-AGI-3 is now clearly framed by ARC Prize and press coverage (MLQ, The Decoder, Softonic, 31 July - 2 Aug) as dependent on non-standard API settings ('retained reasoning' plus 'compaction'); on the official harness Sol scores 13.3% public / 7.8% semi-private, well below Opus 5's 30.2%. Yesterday's forecast already discounted this as a 'claim,' so the harness dispute trims none of the priced-in signal materially - the underlying fact that two labs pushed the generality frontier hard in one week stands either way, and the settings themselves (cross-episode memory retention) are a real capability, just not an apples-to-apples SOTA. (2) Governance: still no public deliverables from the EO 14409 August 1 framework deadline (the classified covered-frontier-model benchmarking process and voluntary 30-day pre-release review remain unpublished as of 4 Aug), and the regime remains expressly voluntary with no licensing or preclearance - so no new brake. (3) No new frontier releases (latest tracked: DeepSeek-V4-Flash on 31 July, Opus 5 on 24 July), no new expert AGI-achieved statements, and no cluster forming toward the 3+ researcher resolution threshold. Central stays 86, CI [72,93].
forecasts.base_rate: Reference class: aggregate forecasts for announcement-based AGI within ~8.4 years. Community medians (Metaculus-style) for AGI/weak-AGI arrival sit in the early 2030s, implying >50% by 2035 and higher for an announcement-based criterion; 2023-24 expert surveys (AI Impacts HLMI) have medians in the 2040s but with fat left tails and consistent shortening each wave; frontier-lab leaders (Altman, Amodei, Hassabis) publicly forecast transformative AI 2026-2030, with Amodei's Davos 2026 'nation of geniuses in a datacenter by 2027' the most aggressive. Announcement-based resolution is materially easier than technical AGI, supporting the premium over capability-only base rates.

factors_up.factor: Generality-benchmark frontier still moving fast: two labs traded ARC-AGI-3 gains within a week in late July (Opus 5 30.2% official; Sol 38.3% with memory-retention settings), from a ~13% ceiling a month earlier
No enacted regulatory brake: EO 14409 framework past its 1 Aug deadline with no published deliverables, and the regime is expressly voluntary; Pacing the Frontier disclaims any current slowdown
Definitional drift (behavioural-AGI framings, industry redefinitions) lowers the bar an announcement must clear by 2035
Lab-leader timelines (Amodei 2027 'nation of geniuses') keep public declaration incentives strong

factors_down.factor: Institutionalised restraint norms (Pacing the Frontier, 1,200+ signatories with corporate endorsements; EO 14409 descendants) could mature into binding international pacing mechanisms within the window

Possible compute, capital, or energy constraints late in the window if current spending proves uneconomic

key_uncertainties: Whether restraint norms (Pacing the Frontier, EO 14409 framework once published) become binding constraints before capabilities arrive
Whether labs facing commercial and governance-clause incentives choose to formally declare AGI or deliberately avoid the term

Revise UP if ARC-AGI-3-class generality benchmarks are effectively saturated under official harnesses by 2027

forecasts.question: Will China initiate a military blockade or invasion of Taiwan before 1 January 2030?
forecasts.key_change: Hold at 8% (CI [4,14]), unchanged from 3 August. Nothing in the last 48 hours fired an update trigger; if anything, the marginal evidence leans quiet. Taiwan's MND morning report for 3 August (globalsecurity.org repost of the ROC MND release) recorded just 1 PLA aircraft sortie, 7 PLAN vessels and 3 official ships around Taiwan, with 1 sortie entering the southwestern ADIZ - lower even than the 2 August figures (5 aircraft, 8 PLAN vessels) cited in yesterday's forecast and well below the 2025 daily norms, consistent with the ongoing post-summit 2026 lull. The key watch item is now imminent rather than resolved: Han Kuang 42's 10-day, 9-night live-fire phase begins tomorrow (5-14 August), and Taipei Times (3 August) confirms it will test US-style methods, first-time M1A2T Abrams participation, the new Littoral Combat Command, and a Phase 1 scenario premised on the PLA concealing attack preparations inside an annual exercise; FDD (28 July) confirms the integrated counter-blockade/quarantine and sea-lane resupply drills that transitioned into Han Kuang in early August. Searches on 4 August found no announced or reported PLA/Eastern Theater Command counter-exercise, no CCG escalation, and no snap 'warning' drills - the most recent encirclement-scale PLA action remains Justice Mission-2025 (late December). The Trump-Xi track is stable: the May 13-15 Beijing summit left the cross-strait status quo formally unchanged (Global Taiwan Institute, CFR), with a possible second summit still in prospect and the delayed $14bn arms package still the main friction point. With activity at or below the recent baseline and no counter-drill materialising yet, the superforecaster discipline is to hold; the next 10 days (through 14 August) are the highest-information window this month, and a PLA counter-exercise exceeding October 2024/December 2025 scale would move the central estimate up 1-2pp, while a quiet Han Kuang passage would support shaving toward 7.
forecasts.base_rate: Reference class: militarised interstate disputes with sustained coercive pressure escalating to blockade or invasion of the specific target within a ~3.5-year window. Historical base rate for deliberate great-power initiation of a war-triggering blockade/invasion in a given half-decade is low single digits (Correlates of War data; 70+ years of cross-strait coercion without assault). Expert elicitations (Atlantic Council 2024-25 surveys, Metaculus) cluster 2030-horizon invasion probability around 8-15%, with blockade-inclusive definitions at the higher end.

forecasts.question: Will UK annual CPI inflation fall below 2.0% for at least one month before 1 January 2027?
forecasts.key_change: Hold at 1% (CI [0,3]), unchanged from 3 Aug. The only material development in the last 24-48 hours is a modest oil retracement: on 3 August Brent fell roughly 5% to just below $84/bbl after President Trump announced that peace talks with Iran would resume, with Saudi Arabia and other regional allies reportedly pressing Washington toward a diplomatic deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. This is directionally favourable for the sub-2% scenario but falls far short of the update trigger set yesterday (Brent below $70 and holding for 3+ weeks before end-September): even after the drop, Brent is still up ~15-20% on late June, and no ceasefire has been signed - talks 'resuming' is a weak signal that has already reversed once in this conflict (the mid-July US-Iran attacks followed earlier de-escalation). Everything else confirms the hold. Cornwall Insight's current October Ofgem cap forecast (~GBP 1,899/yr on the old typical-consumption basis, ~GBP 1,700 on the new TDCV definition, final level to be announced by 26 August) still shows a further rise on July's GBP 1,862, with the cap assessment window (19 May-18 Aug) mostly reflecting war-elevated wholesale prices; the electricity VAT removal only partially offsets. The July CPI print is confirmed for 19 August, with economists still expecting inflation to rise in H2 on energy pass-through. The binding constraint remains the 30 July MPR: central projection ~3.2% CPI in Q4 2026, milder scenario 2.7%, three MPC members voting to hike - sub-2.0% before January remains outside the Bank's entire published scenario range, and with June CPI at 2.6% only the July-November prints can resolve YES. One day of oil softening on a talks headline does not move the five publishable prints; hold.
forecasts.base_rate: Reference class: months where UK CPI printed below 2.0% when the starting rate was 2.5%+ with a central-bank-projected rising path five months from the deadline - essentially unprecedented absent a demand collapse. CPI has printed below 2.0% in only one month since mid-2021 (Sep 2024, 1.7%). A 0.7pp+ fall against a projected ~0.6pp rise within five publishable prints has no post-1997 precedent outside the 2008 and 2014-15 oil crashes, both involving 50%+ oil price declines; the current situation is a partially-retraced upward oil shock (Brent ~$84 on 3 Aug vs ~$88-89 end-July). Sources: ONS CPI series D7G7, BoE July 2026 MPR.

Three MPC members voted to hike on 30 July; consensus expects H2 inflation to rise on energy pass-through

forecasts.question: Will Spider-Man: Brand New Day gross over $1.5B worldwide by 31 December 2026?
forecasts.key_change: Raise to 99% (from 98%). Two pieces of strong new evidence since yesterday justify the move at this extreme end of the scale. First, Monday's finalized actuals (3 Aug, per Deadline, Variety, and THR) revised the opening UP, not down: domestic came in at $360M — surpassing Avengers: Endgame's $357.1M to become the biggest domestic opening in history, versus Sunday's $355M estimate — and the global debut was revised to $932M from $927M. Upward Sunday-to-Monday revisions signal stronger-than-estimated Sunday holds, the opposite of frontloading. Second, and decisive: the film has already crossed $1 billion worldwide (reported 3-4 Aug), the second-fastest film ever to the mark behind only Endgame's five-day record, with Box Office Mojo reporting robust weekday grosses. That means only ~$500M more is needed over the remaining five months — a final multiplier of just ~1.61x on the opening, when the worst multiplier ever recorded for this reference class (maximally frontloaded Endgame) was 2.29x, and industry trackers now openly project a $2.1B+ finish. With an A CinemaScore, 90% RT, biggest-ever opening confirmed in actuals, China delivering ($121M opening frame), and a competition-free August, the only remaining NO paths are systemic shocks (mass theatre closures, geopolitical disruption) or a data/resolution anomaly — worth roughly 1%. This effectively satisfies the spirit of yesterday's pre-registered up-trigger (pace consistent with $1.3B inside two weekends). CI narrows to [97,100]; the second-weekend hold (7-9 Aug) is now confirmation rather than a genuine information event.

Residual 1% covers tracker overstatement risk plus definitional disputes over how Q4 'most recent credible reporting' is summed. Already at the 99 cap per calibration policy; hold.
forecasts.base_rate: Reference class: probability that two companies whose combined ARR already exceeds the threshold on an official-disclosure-only basis (~$72B: Anthropic $47B May Series H + OpenAI ~$25B) fail to be reported above it five months later. Companies with this growth profile (Anthropic $9B end-2025 to $47B official May 2026; OpenAI $20B 2025 to $25B+ and re-accelerating per CFO 29 Jul) essentially never retrench >40% in two quarters absent bankruptcy-level events; base rate of YES >98%. Sources: Anthropic Series H disclosure 28 May 2026, CNBC 29 Jul 2026, The Information, Bloomberg 15 Jul 2026.

forecasts.question: Will UK average annual real GDP growth exceed 1.5% across the 2030s (2030-2039)?
forecasts.key_change: Hold at 34% (CI unchanged at 21-48). Searches on 4 August turned up no material new information in the 3-4 August window; the news flow is a continuation of already-priced developments. Month-end data confirm 10-year gilt yields finished July above 5%, up 28bp on the month, with the rise attributed partly to a ~20% surge in oil prices on Middle East conflict fears reigniting inflation concerns and to the political transition - this validates but does not worsen the 'elevated borrowing costs suppress 2020s investment' channel already embedded in yesterday's forecast. On fiscal policy, Chancellor Healey's public line has firmed toward fiscal discipline (Reuters/TradingView reported yields rising modestly on his cost-of-business and cost-of-living remarks, but sentiment was also supported by the new government 'pledging to maintain fiscal discipline'), which slightly offsets the late-July 'fiscal flexibility' scare; the decisive test remains the autumn Budget and whether the inherited fiscal rules survive. Markets continue to price at least one BoE hike by year-end with ~70% odds of a second - unchanged from the post-MPR picture. On the upside channel, the government's AI-push narrative persists (chancellor's 'fastest AI adoption in G7' pledge, new AI economics institute, government review claims of up to 1.5% annual productivity uplift from full adoption, Lloyds survey showing 56% of AI-adopting firms report productivity gains), but these are aspirational or survey-based rather than measured whole-economy productivity acceleration, and were already reflected in the +5pp AI factor. No change to any structural anchor: OBR (March 2026 EFO, potential output growth revised marginally lower), BoE (~1.4% supply growth), and OECD (~1%) all remain at or below the 1.5% bar, and the Treasury's July survey of independent forecasters averages just 1.0% growth for both 2026 and 2027. A daily hold is the calibrated response.
forecasts.base_rate: Reference class: UK decade-average real GDP growth - 2.9% (1980s), 2.1% (1990s), 1.8% (2000s incl. GFC), 2.0% (2010s), and an estimated ~1.3-1.5% for the 2020s to date; post-2008 trend growth has sat near 1-1.5% for 15+ years. Institutional long-run projections cluster below the bar: OBR trend downgraded toward ~1.5% or below after the March 2026 productivity downgrade (potential output growth marginally lowered again on weaker net migration), BoE potential ~1.4%, OECD long-term ~1%, and real GDP per person forecast at ~1.1%/yr for 2026-2030. Exceeding 1.5% for a full decade average therefore requires a productivity regime change (e.g. AI diffusion) or sustained above-trend catch-up. Sources: ONS ABMI series, OBR EFO March 2026, OECD long-term scenarios.

factors_up.factor: BoE scenarios converge to 1.6-1.7% annual growth by 2028-29, giving positive momentum into the decade
Potential AI/technology-driven productivity acceleration not embedded in official trend estimates, with active government adoption push (G7-fastest-adopter pledge, AI economics institute)
Post-energy-shock normalisation plus possible catch-up growth early in the 2030s

factors_down.factor: Official potential-growth estimates (BoE ~1.4%, OECD ~1%, OBR downgraded again in March 2026) all at or below the 1.5% bar
G7-highest gilt yields (10yr >5% at end-July, +28bp on the month), oil-driven inflation risk and priced BoE hikes suppress 2020s investment and the capital stock entering the 2030s
Demographics: shrinking workforce growth, lower net migration assumptions, and rising old-age dependency through the 2030s

key_uncertainties: Whether AI adoption produces a measurable UK productivity acceleration by the early 2030s, beyond survey-reported firm-level gains
Whether the Healey Treasury's autumn Budget maintains the inherited fiscal rules or shifts toward Burnham's 'fiscal flexibility', and the resulting gilt-market path
Long-run energy costs given the Middle East conflict's oil-price shock
Migration policy and labour-supply growth through the 2030s
Whether ONS measurement and revisions shift the decade mean around the 1.5% threshold
update_triggers: Revise UP if OBR or BoE upgrade UK potential/trend growth to 1.5%+ in a future forecast round
Revise UP if UK productivity growth sustains 1.5%+ annualised for 4+ consecutive quarters
Revise UP if gilt yields fall materially (10-year below 4%) easing the investment constraint
Revise DOWN if the autumn Budget abandons fiscal rules and triggers a sustained gilt selloff (10-year above 5.5%)
Revise DOWN if the 2020s decade average finishes below 1.2%, indicating entrenched sub-trend momentum
Revise DOWN if measured AI productivity effects disappoint in US/UK data through 2027-28
